name: TD Friends of the Environment Foundation Grant

funder.name: TD Friends of the Environment Foundation

summary: Grants for Canadian charities, municipalities, schools and Indigenous groups running environmental projects such as park revitalization, schoolyard greening, tree planting with native species and citizen science. Does not fund capital costs, operating costs or research.

amount.note: No set minimum or maximum; most grants fall in this range

eligibility.rule: Charity applicants have a Charitable Registration Number
Project is not underway when applying
Project is not a research project
Community gardens address at least one environmental issue
The school applies for education projects involving planting, gardens or physical changes to school grounds
Applicant organisation is located in Canada
Outdoor classroom or nature play projects changing school grounds need school board approval

documents: Plant list for tree planting and greening projects
School participation confirmation if an environmental organisation will present there

status.quote: 2027 Submission Deadlines Winter submission Summer submission Submission deadline December 15, 2026 June 15

deadline.quote: 2027 Submission Deadlines Winter submission Summer submission Submission deadline December 15, 2026 June 15

applicant_types.quote: Organizations eligible to receive funding: Registered Canadian charities with a Charitable Registration Number (CRN) Educational institutions (primary/secondary/post-secondary) Municipalities Indigenous groups/communities

geography.quote: TD FEF can only fund projects taking place in Canada.

access.quote: All grant applications must be submitted online.

window.quote: 2027 Submission Deadlines Winter submission Summer submission Submission deadline December 15, 2026 June 15

amount.quote: there is no set minimum or maximum amount for which you can apply. However, the majority of TD FEF grants are between $2,000 and $8,000.

effort.quote: All grant applications must be submitted online.
All applications for funding are reviewed by one of six Regional Advisory Boards.

eligibility.quote: Registered Canadian charities with a Charitable Registration Number (CRN)
TD FEF cannot provide funding for projects already underway.
Projects occurring on private land with no public access
Community Garden projects need to contain a focus on at least one environmental issue in order to be eligible for funding.
If the project involves planting, gardens or any physical alterations to school grounds, the application must be submitted by the school.
Is the organization located in Canada?
Are there changes being made to the school grounds? If yes, school board approval is required.

documents.quote: Applicants must attach a budget to their application form.
Please provide a plant list in your application detailing what native or non-native plants will be used and why (e.g., increase pollinators, provide shade, etc.)
If the applicant is an environmental organization presenting to the school, please include confirmation of participation from the school(s).
